simple.meaning: קַרְדֹּם (qardôm) is a Hebrew word meaning “an axe.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קַרְדֹּם (H7134) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 9:48, with occurrences in Judges, 1 Samuel, Psalms, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קַרְדֹּם (H7134) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קַרְדֹּם (H7134) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קַרְדֹּם (qardôm) / H7134 is traced through Judges 9:48, 1 Samuel 13:20, 1 Samuel 13:21, Psalms 74:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech took an ax in his hand, and cut down a bough from the trees, and took it up, and laid it on his shoulder. Then he said to the people who were with him, “What you have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done!”

but all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his own plowshare, mattock, ax, and sickle.
The price was one payim† A payim (or pim) was 2/3 shekel of silver, or 0.26 ounces, or 7.6 grams each to sharpen mattocks, plowshares, pitchforks, axes, and goads.
They behaved like men wielding axes,
Its sound will go like the serpent;

definitions.full: H7134. qardom [ קַרְדֹּם ] noun [masculine] axe (√ unknown; compare Late Hebrew קַרְדֹּם double hoe ,one side of which could split wood, Vogelst Land writhsch.37 ; Arabic , adze is loan-word according to Frä 84 ); — suffix קַרְדֻמּוֺ 1Sam 13:20 + Judg 9:48 (so probably read for הַקַּרְדֻּמוֺתּ , A ᵐ5 L τ. ἀξίνημ , GFM Bu Now); plural קַרְדֻּמִּים 1Sam 13:21 , קַרְדֻּמוֺת Jer 46:22 ; Psa 74:5
